root_cause.text: The SM8450 interconnect topology still contained two `qcom_icc_node.link_nodes` entries using old static master IDs after the switch to dynamic IDs, so `icc_link_nodes()` was given an invalid destination-node pointer and dereferenced NULL during probe.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `qhs_compute_cfg.link_nodes` from `{ MASTER_CDSP_NOC_CFG }` to `{ &qhm_nsp_noc_config }` and `qhs_lpass_cfg.link_nodes` from `{ MASTER_CNOC_LPASS_AG_NOC }` to `{ &qhm_config_noc }`, and the commit message says “The change to dynamic IDs for SM8450 platform interconnects left two links unconverted” causing a NULL pointer dereference in `icc_link_nodes()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Update the compute interconnect node to reference the correct linked node in the QCOM ICC topology.
intent_record.what: The `link_nodes` initializer in `qhs_compute_cfg` was changed from `MASTER_CDSP_NOC_CFG` to `&qhm_nsp_noc_config`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the interconnect node `qhs_compute_cfg` will now link to a different downstream node, changing the topology used for interconnect path resolution and traffic routing.

intent_record.intent_summary: Update the LPASS config interconnect link to point at the correct NOC node.
intent_record.what: In the qcom_icc_node definition for `qhs_lpass_cfg`, the single entry in `link_nodes` was changed from `MASTER_CNOC_LPASS_AG_NOC` to `&qhm_config_noc`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the LPASS config interconnect node will now route its link through the `qhm_config_noc` node instead of the previous CNOC LPASS AG NOC master endpoint, changing the connectivity/topology used by the interconnect graph.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 51513bec806fbe1cf9254baed97f115a480bbb53
Author: Dmitry Baryshkov <dmitry.baryshkov@oss.qualcomm.com>
Date:   Fri Oct 31 16:45:37 2025 +0200

    interconnect: qcom: sm8450: convert to dynamic IDs
    
    Stop using fixed and IDs and covert the platform to use dynamic IDs for
    the interconnect. This gives more flexibility and also allows us to drop
    the .num_links member, saving from possible errors related to it being
    not set or set incorrectly.
    
    Signed-off-by: Dmitry
bic_trace_step.reason: The shown snippet is sufficient because it directly contains the SM8450 topology definitions and the link setup that would trigger the issue. However, the vulnerable construct described in the root cause is absent here: the commit converts many nodes from fixed IDs to dynamic IDs by removing lines like `.id = SM8450_MASTER_*` and replacing `.links = { ... }` with `.link_nodes = { &... }`, e.g. `qhm_qspi` now has `".link_nodes = { &qns_a1noc_snoc }"` and `sm8450_*` descriptors now set `".alloc_dyn_id = true"`. That indicates the intended fix is already present in this version. The bad old static master-ID references that caused `icc_link_nodes()` to get an invalid destination pointer are not present in the converted nodes shown, so `has_bug` is NO and `is_fixed` is YES.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet clearly shows the vulnerable pattern: links are created directly from the static topology via `icc_link_create(node, qnodes[i]->links[j]);` inside `qnoc_probe()`, with no validation that the destination node exists or that the link ID matches the post-dynamic-ID mapping. The root cause mentions stale static master IDs causing `icc_link_nodes()` to receive an invalid destination-node pointer and dereference NULL during probe. In this commit, several nodes still use raw link IDs in `.links = { ... }`, and the probe code blindly iterates over them. There is no fix present here such as validating or translating link targets before creating links, so this commit contains the bug and does not contain the fix.
